A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same batching study despite the revised title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original CPU/GPU timing, batching statistics, recompilation counts, and test-RMSE experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds PaiNN/static-constant comparisons and four-GPU compatibility observations.

M1.justification: The four batching algorithms and three GNN architectures are retained. Appendix F discusses a possible common-padding workaround for multiple GPUs, without adopting it in the evaluated methods.

E1.justification: QM9 internal-energy and AFLOW enthalpy tasks remain unchanged. Appendix F adds a four-GPU compatibility scenario requiring matching per-device batch shapes, beyond v2's CPU and single-GPU evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds static-constant to PaiNN comparisons on both datasets at batch size 16. It also adds dynamic batching to the AFLOW/MPEU batch-16 static-constant comparison, where v2's table omitted it.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces four-GPU testing using JAX pmap and its equal-shape requirement. The principal batch sizes, two-million-step timing budget, shorter CPU experiments, preprocessing, metrics, and model sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds an analysis of static batching failures under multi-GPU execution and quantifies AFLOW's distribution tails. Existing recompilation, training-duration, mean-versus-median, CPU, and learning analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Section 8 newly reports estimated excess kurtosis greater than one for AFLOW's node and edge distributions. The ten-run timing design, mean/median reporting, pairwise Student's t-tests, and p-value thresholds are unchanged.

E6.justification: New static-constant PaiNN results in Table 1 include 47.39 ms combined time on AFLOW versus 3.79 ms for dynamic batching, supporting the added 12.5x comparison. Appendix F reports approximately 90% and 99% shape mismatches for static-2N and static-64. Earlier table values and matched plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: V3 removes the explicit background full-batch loss definition and gradient-descent update formula from v2 Section 2, Equations 1–2. The seven model equations remain, renumbered in Appendix A; no new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction and discussion now distinguish the retained 2.7x comparison from a 12.5x comparison against static-constant. They also make recommending dynamic batching and generally discouraging static-constant central contributions, substantially changing the practical message.

C2.justification: V2 recommends benchmarking algorithms for each new dataset/model; v3 generally recommends dynamic batching. V3 adds conditions under which static-constant's robustness may justify its cost, explains its padding overhead more fully, and documents static batching's multi-GPU applicability limits.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds technical information about JAX pmap, per-device shape constraints, and a possible padding workaround. The existing hardware inventory, timing instrumentation, and listed software/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds DeCarlo's kurtosis reference and graph-background citations to Koller/Friedman, Liu/Zhou, and Speckhard (2025). It removes Hastie and the Bajaj/Wan large-graph partitioning discussion. Section 3 also explicitly presents static-2N and static-64 as introduced here.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper, rewrites contributions and substantial parts of the preliminaries/results narrative, compresses related work, reorders models and hardware sections, and moves model equations and additional pseudocode into appendices. The separate impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. V3 merges histogram panels, combines three models' timing plots in Figure 4 with rescaled axes, promotes the running-average plot into the main text, expands Table 1, and revises captions and figure placement.

improvement.justification: The added PaiNN/static-constant comparisons make the baseline assessment more complete, while Appendix F clarifies practical multi-GPU failure conditions. These provide a limited improvement in usefulness and applicability guidance. The reorganization introduces a mean/median cross-reference error for Figures 6–7 in Section 8, but this does not outweigh those gains.
